text: The death is announced of Sir Squire Bancroft, the noted actor.

label: text
text: [Sir Squire Bancroft, KL., Hon. LL.D., was born in London on May 14, 1841; and married in 1867, Marie Effe Wilton, the famous actress, who died in 1921. They had one son, who married a daughter of the late Sir John Hare. Sir Squire Bancroft was educated at private schools in England and France. He first appeared on the stage at Birmingham in 1861; and acted afterward at the leading provincial theatres with all the prominent "stars" of the stage. For twenty years he was manager of the old Prince of Wales's and Haymarket Theatres, during which the modern revival of stage was started. He retired from an exceptional career of successful management in 1885, but noted afterward with trying. He was kifighted by Queen Victoria for notable services to his profession. Sir Squire devoted much time to "rendings" for Hospitals throughout the country, and by which he raised £20,000. Besides being President of the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art, he was a member of the Lord Chamberlain's Advisory Board for the Licensing of Plays. He was the joint-author of "Mr. and Mrs. Bancroft On and Off the Stage," Written by "Themselves," and author of "The Bancroft Recollections of Sixty Years."

label: text
text: Mr. Frank Kellogg has sent a formal notification that "Americans will not participate in the World Court Conference at Geneva on September 1 to the American Legation at Berne for delivery to the League.

label: text
text: Mr. Kellogg says he thought that it would be a matter for regret if the Council did anything to create an impression that there were substantial difficulties on the way of direct communication with the various signatories. The American Government does not consider that any new agreement is necessary to give effect to the conditions and reservations on the basis of which America is prepared to adhere to the World Court.

label: text
text: The American refusal to participate in the World Court Conference has produced disappointment in League Circles, though it is felt that the Conference will be held on September 1 in spite of that. None of the signatories has replied to the League's invitation to attend, and it is thought that the matter must now come up at the June session of the Council.

text: The French and Turkish Press are apprehensive concerning Signor Mussolini's intentions in North-West Africa and Asia Minor, respectively.

label: text
text: There have been reports of a Grneco-Italian Pact and Greek military preparations in which Italy is assisting, and on the top of this comes the news that the Turks are mobilising, and the Turkish news papers give prominence to rumours of a possible conflict with Italy, though they insist that there is "nothing abnormal in the situation."

label: text
text: Mussolini's visit to Tripoli has been undoubtedly responsible for the most alarming conjectures, including his making a bid for leadership of the Arab world, and also his determination to secure for Italy a role equal to that of France and Spain in Tangier.

label: text
text: Signor Mussolini was oratorically attacked in the Senate by Senator

label: text
text: Thomas J. Walsh (Democrat, Helena, Montana) declaring that his Tripoli trip bristled with belli-cose bluster. The Kaiser never rattled his sword more ominously.

label: text
text: Senator Walsh contended that approval of the Italian debt settlement would simply assist Mussolini, "the Supreme Dictator," to arrange his finances so that he could precipitate another war or bluster about it until the fear of such purpose was general.
